what_happened: In job 67fa (a code job), the user corrected Athena's first reading before work began. The job is about a low-disk stop and its retry. The reading's test design did not match the code. The user made five changes. (1) The test must pass the first disk gate, which runs before the checks, and stop only at the second gate, which runs before the verifier. That means giving it enough free space for the first gate and less for the second. (2) An interrupted process stays a resumable cause, as the request said. (3) The text must say the retry still runs the reader. (4) The reading must reuse disk::is_environment_reason instead of a near-duplicate. (5) Resume must be asserted by counting planner and producer invocations, not reads of the free-space function.
cause: The reading stage designs a test from the general idea of the feature, not from the code's actual gates and helpers. Nothing makes it name the order of operations, the existing function to reuse, or the observable that proves a property. A free-space read is the easiest thing to count, and a new helper is easier to write than finding the old one. The reading is accepted without that check. Only the user, who knows the code layout, catches it. The earlier case in this class (dhh0) was corrected for that one job only, and the correction was not carried into the reading stage.
prevention: Add a required step to the reading stage and its critic for any code job with a behavior test. Before the reading is accepted, it must contain a short code survey. For each test criterion, the survey names (a) the entry point and the ordered gates the run passes through, and which gate the test must stop at; (b) any existing function that already does the job, which must be reused; (c) the observable that proves the property, such as call counts of the stages that must or must not run, not reads of an internal helper. The critic rejects a reading when any of these is missing or contradicts the code. This replaces one-off user corrections with a check that every reading goes through.
proposed_request: Add a code-survey requirement to Athena's reading stage for code jobs that have behavior tests. Outcome: a reading is not accepted unless, for each test criterion, it names three things. First, the entry point and the ordered gates the run passes through, and the gate at which the test must stop. Second, any existing function that already does the job, which the reading must reuse instead of adding a near-duplicate. Third, an observable that proves the property directly, such as how many times the planner, producer and reader were invoked, and not reads of an internal helper such as the free-space function. Add the same three checks to the reading critic's rules so it rejects a reading that omits them or contradicts the code. Acceptance: (1) a test with a fixture reading that omits the gate order is refused and names what is missing; (2) a fixture reading that proposes a new helper where an existing one is present, such as disk::is_environment_reason, is refused; (3) a fixture reading that asserts resume by reading the free-space function is refused; (4) a complete fixture reading is accepted; (5) replay the new rule against the last 50 real accepted readings in records and list any it would newly refuse, as the refusal-rule replay requires; (6) the prompt budgets test and the banned-word boundary test still pass.
